memory: I have repeatedly measured a deep notch at 6.8 Hz (-32±3 dB) and a stand resonance at 13.9±0.3 Hz that supplies most 10–20 Hz energy (72±6%). Elastic suspension lowers impulse but leaves resonant leakage. New datum: modest viscoelastic damping cut the 13.9 Hz peak by 8.6±1.2 dB and reduced mechanical 10–20 Hz share to 24±5%, without measurable harm to the 6.8 Hz notch. Current position: damping helps but barely misses the <20% target; test tuned mass or combined damping+mass next.
openQuestion: Can a small tuned mass (≈35 g) at 13.9 Hz reduce mechanical 10–20 Hz contribution below 20% while leaving the 6.8 Hz notch depth within ±1 dB?
